prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of the incretin hormone GLP-1 and its action on insulin secretion and appetite, which enabled incretin-based therapies for diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: All six of us placed B046 first, but that agreement is not the argument. The argument is that GLP-1 is a complete arc from hormone physiology (proglucagon processing, the active GLP-1(7-36) form, glucose-dependent insulin secretion, effects on appetite and gastric emptying) to drugs that now change the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal outcome benefit shown in large trials. Originality, clarity of the discovery chain, durability and breadth of impact are all strong, and the work has been independently confirmed for decades, so there is no maturity concern. Holst for the physiology and secretion, Drucker for the mechanism and therapeutic proof of concept, and Mojsov for identification and synthesis of the active peptide best represent the discovery side within the three-person limit.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution, not merit. Mojsov's priority relative to Habener and other early peptide groups is historically contested, and Habener is not among the credited names, so a three-person prize could be criticised as incomplete. Excluding Lotte Bjerre Knudsen means the prize rewards physiology over the long-acting analogues that actually reached patients, and a reader could say the citation underweights the drug development that produced the clinical impact. I consider this a real weakness of the configuration, not a settled question.

responses.point: The chair ranked B031 (unfolded protein response, Mori and Walter) second, as a clean two-person discovery of a new organelle-to-nucleus signalling logic, and ranked B015 (TOR) third, with Hall and Schreiber.
responses.response: I agree that B031 is the cleanest attribution on the shortlist and that its mechanistic originality is high. I ranked it fourth, below B040 and B049, because its therapeutic translation is still early and both CAR-T and optogenetics have changed practice or experimental method more broadly. On B015 I qualify the choice of Schreiber over Sabatini. Schreiber's rapamycin-FKBP12 chemistry is the second pillar, but the mammalian mTOR and nutrient-sensing mechanism is arguably the bigger part of what is now taught, so I do not think leaving Sabatini out is obvious. That is a reason B015 is not my preferred second configuration.

responses.point: Sandberg ranked B040 second but limited it to June and Sadelain, judging the decisive CAR engineering to sit with them rather than Rosenberg. He also ranked B024 (massively parallel sequencing) third as an enabling technology.
responses.response: I side with Sandberg on the two-person CAR-T configuration. Sadelain's costimulated CAR design and June's clinical CD19 translation carry the discovery, and Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer and TIL work is a forerunner and not the CAR itself. I had a three-name version in my opening and now think that was too generous. I disagree with him on B024. Sequencing technology has enabled much of my own field, but that is exactly why I distrust my own enthusiasm. It is an enabling invention with contested platform origins, and Mayer, Balasubramanian and Klenerman leave out the pyrosequencing and polony lineages. I would not put it ahead of a physiological or clinical discovery.

responses.point: Perlmann ranked B046 first but treated Mojsov's credit as historically contested. He ranked B040 only seventh because the credited set lacks Eshhar, and he put B015 with Hall and Schreiber at third.
responses.response: Perlmann's point about missing Eshhar is fair and I carry it as a real qualification, but I do not think it sinks B040. A committee can credit the clinically decisive costimulated designs and their translation without claiming to resolve the earliest chimeric-receptor priority. His doubt about Mojsov applies to B046 as well, and I share it. Even so, I would keep her in. Without the identification and synthesis of the active peptide, the physiology and the drug story lose their first link. If the committee cannot settle this, the fallback is to recognise Holst and Drucker, which would be thinner but still defensible.

responses.point: El-Manira placed B049 (optogenetics) second, with Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann, on the originality and lasting reach of the method across circuit neuroscience, and treated B046 as the most defensible first choice.
responses.response: I share the view that optogenetics is among the most original contributions on the list, and I ranked it third. My hesitation is with allocation. Six credited people cannot fit into three, and dropping Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck is a serious cut in a story where discovery and neuronal deployment are tightly interlinked. Clinical translation is also still early. I do not accept that this makes it a lesser discovery. It does make it a poorer fit for this year than B046, where the three-name choice is contested only at the margins, and I would keep it as an alternative and not as a second prize part.

uncertainties: Whether the committee can settle Mojsov's priority against Habener and other early GLP-1 peptide groups from the supplied evidence.
Whether to credit Lotte Bjerre Knudsen for drug development, which would require dropping one of the three physiology names.
Whether a second prize part (B040 with June and Sadelain) would improve the configuration or only dilute a strong single-achievement prize.
How the committee should treat the missing original chimeric-receptor contributor (Eshhar) if B040 is chosen.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for B046, B040 or B049. My documented spatial-transcriptomics and single-cell work, and eight recorded co-authored works with Rickard Sandberg, are not tied to any shortlisted candidate. If B024 (massively parallel sequencing) were seriously considered, I would flag my methodological proximity to sequencing technology and ask the committee to weigh whether recusal is needed.
